rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act – ban on criminal-history inquiries before a conditional offer
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record, orally, in writing or on an application, until after making a conditional offer. The only exceptions are methamphetamine production on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex-offender registration. Before accepting any application fee, the provider must disclose in writing whether criminal history is reviewed and that the applicant may submit evidence of inaccuracies, rehabilitation or other mitigating factors.
rules.key_value: No criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer
rules.quoted_span:
A housing
provider
shall not make any oral or written inquiry
regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.coverage_text: Rental dwelling units offered for rent by a housing provider for residential purposes, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units. Providers may consider methamphetamine manufacture or production on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex-offender registration before the offer.
rules.penalty: Penalties are imposed by the Division on Civil Rights: up to $1,000 for a first violation, up to $5,000 if there is one other violation within five years, and up to $10,000 if there are two or more other violations within seven years. The director may also order cease and desist, remedial housing offers and return of the application fee, and may direct up to $1,000 of the penalty to the applicant. No private court action is allowed.
rules.extraction_note: The effective date is calculated from §14: the act takes effect on the first day of the seventh month next following enactment, and it was approved June 18, 2021. The document does not state 2022-01-01 explicitly.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act – post-offer criminal record limits, lookback periods and withdrawal procedure
rules.requirement: Housing providers may never consider arrests or charges without conviction, or expunged, pardoned, vacated, juvenile or sealed records. After a conditional offer, they may consider only listed serious crimes and recent indictable convictions: 6 years for first degree, 4 years for second or third degree, and 1 year for fourth degree. An offer may be withdrawn only after an individualized assessment shows, by preponderance of the evidence, that withdrawal is necessary for a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest, and the provider must give written reasons and an opportunity to appeal.
rules.key_value: Lookback 6 yrs (1st degree) / 4 yrs (2nd-3rd degree) / 1 yr (4th degree)
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider may withdraw a
conditional offer based on an applicant's criminal record only if the housing
provider determines, by preponderance of the evidence, that the withdrawal is
necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.
rules.coverage_text: Rental dwelling units offered for rent by a housing provider for residential purposes, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units. Convictions for murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, specified sexual offenses, or crimes requiring lifetime sex-offender registration may be considered without a lookback limit.
rules.penalty: Penalties are imposed by the Division on Civil Rights: up to $1,000 for a first violation, up to $5,000 if there is one other violation within five years, and up to $10,000 if there are two or more other violations within seven years. The director may also order cease and desist, remedial housing offers and return of the application fee, and may direct up to $1,000 of the penalty to the applicant.
rules.extraction_note: The effective date is calculated from §14 (first day of the seventh month after the June 18, 2021 approval) and is not stated explicitly. Applicants may request, within 30 days of withdrawal, the information the provider relied on, which must be provided free of charge within 10 days.
